signals.title: Midwest diesel rises 5.1% in a week
signals.summary: EIA’s 14 September Midwest diesel benchmark is $6.250/gal, up $0.304 from $5.946. Watershed’s actual surcharge exposure is unknown.
signals.factorRationale: Retail diesel ↑ → carrier fuel surcharges → delivered costs. Exposure 75 assumes truck reliance; severity 70 reflects a 5.1% weekly move. Confidence 70, persistence 70, velocity 80, dependency 80 and substitutability 35 are provisional analyst judgments.
signals.causalPath: Retail diesel ↑ → carrier fuel surcharges → delivered costs. Exposure 75 assumes truck reliance; severity 70 reflects a 5.1% weekly move. Confidence 70, persistence 70, velocity 80, dependency 80 and substitutability 35 are provisional analyst judgments.
signals.verify: Freight contracts, surcharge lag, outbound miles and customer pass-through.
signals.action: Ask logistics and finance to quantify surcharge sensitivity for the next shipping cycle.
signals.trigger: Another >5% weekly rise or contracted transport costs >5% above plan.

signals.title: Grain outlook tightens; specialty basis still unknown
signals.summary: September WASDE projects U.S. total-grain ending stocks of 62.92 Mt versus 65.03 Mt in August. That is a broad context signal, not a popcorn forecast.
signals.factorRationale: Broad grain balance → potential feed/grain pricing → formula costs. All seven factors are uncalibrated proxies (45/55/45/80/45/55/60); popping-grade corn and food-grade contracts can diverge materially.
signals.causalPath: Broad grain balance → potential feed/grain pricing → formula costs. All seven factors are uncalibrated proxies (45/55/45/80/45/55/60); popping-grade corn and food-grade contracts can diverge materially.
signals.verify: Actual grains, specification basis, origin, contracts and inventory cover.
signals.action: Track supplier quotations before changing coverage or formulations.
signals.trigger: Two relevant supplier quotes worsen >10%, or verified cover falls below the approved operating threshold.

signals.title: Traceability planning requires a product-form decision
signals.summary: FDA describes a proposed extension and a congressional direction not to enforce the rule before 20 July 2028. Applicability still depends on covered food and form.
signals.factorRationale: Covered receiving/transformation → KDE/CTE obligations → systems and partner coordination. Scope is not established for Watershed; factors 55/65/65/90/25/70/60 reflect planning exposure rather than a violation.
signals.causalPath: Covered receiving/transformation → KDE/CTE obligations → systems and partner coordination. Scope is not established for Watershed; factors 55/65/65/90/25/70/60 reflect planning exposure rather than a violation.
signals.verify: Food Traceability List applicability at each process stage; exemptions; customer contractual dates.
signals.action: Quality and IT should map covered inputs and data exchanges, retaining product-specific legal review.
signals.trigger: Final regulatory change, customer deadline, or a confirmed gap in an applicable traceability process.

signals.title: Pet formats offer a qualified commercial opening
signals.summary: APPA projects $69.7bn of pet-food and treat sales for 2026. This does not establish unit growth or freeze-dried segment growth.
signals.factorRationale: Pet-category spending → candidate launch budgets → topper/inclusion projects suited to advertised capabilities. Factors 70/60/45/85/45/65/65 reflect an unvalidated sales hypothesis, not Watershed revenue.
signals.causalPath: Pet-category spending → candidate launch budgets → topper/inclusion projects suited to advertised capabilities. Factors 70/60/45/85/45/65/65 reflect an unvalidated sales hypothesis, not Watershed revenue.
signals.verify: Premium segment units, brand launch plans, current capacity and qualified process fit.
signals.action: Build a small list of qualified topper/inclusion prospects and test demand before reserving capacity.
signals.trigger: Documented customer briefs and trial conversion, with confirmed available capacity and validated safety controls.
signals.dateNote: APPA projection publication date unverified; baseline evidence, not a new event on retrieval day.

signals.title: Popcorn expansion is an opportunity to verify
signals.summary: Deer Creek’s public directory now lists Aunt Em’s / Heartland together. The reported equipment transition remains unverified as completed.
signals.factorRationale: Announced process additions → possible new formats → private-label prospects. Factors 70/65/60/85/40/75/60 assume qualification work; no incremental capacity is counted as operational.
signals.causalPath: Announced process additions → possible new formats → private-label prospects. Factors 70/65/60/85/40/75/60 assume qualification work; no incremental capacity is counted as operational.
signals.verify: Equipment ownership, commissioning, production qualification and available slots.
signals.action: Confirm the production milestone before offering new formats or delivery commitments.
signals.trigger: Verified commissioned capacity plus a qualified customer opportunity.

signals.title: Baby-food lead guidance has a material scope exclusion
signals.summary: The FDA final guidance excludes grain-based and freeze-dried snacks. It must not be applied automatically to every toddler product.
signals.factorRationale: SKU classification → applicable contaminant requirements/customer specifications → testing and release criteria. Low velocity 20 reflects an existing rule, not new contamination. Other factors are analytical prioritization.
signals.causalPath: SKU classification → applicable contaminant requirements/customer specifications → testing and release criteria. Low velocity 20 reflects an existing rule, not new contamination. Other factors are analytical prioritization.
signals.verify: Each SKU’s form, age positioning, state rules and customer specifications.
signals.action: Keep contaminant controls; have Quality document the correct guidance scope by SKU.
signals.trigger: Changed FDA/state requirements or an actual out-of-spec result; then use the approved food-safety response process.

forecasts.question: Will Midwest on-highway diesel exceed $6.250/gal for the week of 12 October 2026?
forecasts.resolutionRule: Use the first EIA release reporting the week of 2026-10-12; strict greater-than $6.250. Missing/delayed release stays unresolved.
forecasts.rationale: Recent benchmark momentum; no fitted forecasting model. Baseline judgment, not a commodity trade recommendation.

forecasts.question: Will October WASDE project U.S. total-grain ending stocks below 65.03 Mt for 2026/27?
forecasts.resolutionRule: Compare the October 2026 WASDE 2026/27 U.S. total-grain ending-stocks forecast in million metric tons with 65.03. Do not substitute corn-only data.
forecasts.rationale: September forecast is below August, but the next revision is uncertain.

forecasts.question: Will a primary public source confirm the Deer Creek equipment transition is operational by 31 March 2027?
forecasts.resolutionRule: Outcome 1 requires a dated company/government statement explicitly confirming operational completion by the horizon. Outcome 0 is failure of public confirmation by the horizon, not proof the project failed.
forecasts.rationale: Announced intent and directory evidence support progress, but no commissioning record was found.

hypotheses.title: Higher dairy prices threaten yogurt-melt margins.
hypotheses.evidenceFor: Advertised yogurt products create a plausible solids-cost channel.
hypotheses.evidenceAgainst: Pass-through, contracted inputs and actual category contribution are unknown.
hypotheses.indicators: Milk/solids quotes; product contribution; pass-through lag
hypotheses.falsification: No material margin change across two sustained >10% input-price moves.

hypotheses.title: Premium pet spending increases demand for freeze-dried toppers.
hypotheses.evidenceFor: Advertised toppers align with a substantial pet category.
hypotheses.evidenceAgainst: Dollar spend can reflect inflation; premium units and Watershed order mix are unknown.
hypotheses.indicators: Segment units; launches; briefs; conversion to orders
hypotheses.falsification: Three periods of segment growth with no comparable qualified lead/order response.

hypotheses.title: Drought in a key fruit origin affects Watershed within 60 days.
hypotheses.evidenceFor: Fruit processing establishes a possible channel.
hypotheses.evidenceAgainst: No key source region or inventory cover is verified.
hypotheses.indicators: Verified origin; drought; crop yield; contracted cover
hypotheses.falsification: Verified sourcing lies elsewhere or contracted supply/cover prevents a measurable 60-day effect.

hypotheses.title: Popcorn expansion adds corn, oils, cheese-powder, film and promotion exposures.
hypotheses.evidenceFor: Announced popcorn transition and process growth.
hypotheses.evidenceAgainst: Commissioning, actual formulas and customer terms remain unknown.
hypotheses.indicators: Operating milestone; formulas; packaging specifications; retail promotion orders
hypotheses.falsification: No production transition or relevant ingredients/formats in the confirmed portfolio.

hypotheses.title: Top Fox creates differentiated seed and roasting exposure.
hypotheses.evidenceFor: Seed products and the brand’s farming origin are public.
hypotheses.evidenceAgainst: Origins, owned vs bought inputs and manufacturing allocation are unknown.
hypotheses.indicators: Food-grade seed harvest; origin concentration; roasting yield
hypotheses.falsification: Verified production and input model has no incremental seed/roasting exposure.

hypotheses.title: Automation lowers labor exposure but raises OT and specialized-maintenance dependency.
hypotheses.evidenceFor: Maintenance and engineering are public capabilities.
hypotheses.evidenceAgainst: Automation intensity and measured labor productivity are unknown.
hypotheses.indicators: Labor hours/unit; maintenance delays; software inventory; vendor dependency
hypotheses.falsification: Automation adds no measurable labor saving or dependency after controlled comparison.

claims.statement: Watershed describes itself as family-owned and names Jeremy Zobrist as CEO.
claims.note: The statement does not identify equity percentages or all owners.

claims.statement: Watershed Foods LLC and The Manna Group LLC jointly signed an Illinois EDGE agreement.
claims.note: Co-participation establishes a relationship, not a parent/subsidiary direction.

claims.statement: The state agreement identifies the project at 202 North Ford Street, Gridley. Current company recruiting describes Gridley freeze-drying.
The 2024 project proposed depositing, freezing, traying, freeze-drying and packaging additions, with a 31 December 2026 benchmark.
claims.note: Completion and installed line status remain unverified.

claims.statement: Watershed says its origins were supplying ingredients to large cereal producers.
The public company profile gives 2004 as the founding year.
claims.note: Self-reported profile; formation record not retrieved.

claims.statement: A public company profile lists 2221 W College Avenue and Bloomington-Normal headquarters.
claims.note: Office/presence lead. Current headquarters designation and function need primary corroboration; do not replace Gridley manufacturing.

claims.statement: Watershed’s careers page describes baking and popping in greater Milwaukee.
claims.note: Street address, legal operator and line allocation are not established. Do not confuse Thrive’s Oak Creek plant with Watershed.

claims.statement: Top Fox identifies Jeremy Zobrist as founder/owner and lists a Congerville contact address.
claims.note: 1781 US Highway 150 is a public business contact location; exact operational footprint not established.

claims.statement: CFO Derek Karr described Top Fox and Aunt Em’s as Watershed sister companies.
claims.note: Relationship described in a January interview; legal holding structure not established.

claims.statement: Watershed planned to purchase Aunt Em’s equipment and transition operations to Heartland Food Solutions during 2026.
claims.note: No verified closing date or completed expansion.

claims.statement: The village directory lists Aunt Em’s / Heartland at 404 E. First Avenue.
Derek Karr was identified as CFO of Watershed and Heartland.
claims.note: Dated role attribution, not an evergreen executive roster.

claims.statement: Watershed advertises freeze-dried, baked, roasted and popped platforms.
Public offerings span yogurt melts, fruit/vegetables, supplement blends, pet toppers, baked kibble/treats, nuts/seeds, legumes and popcorn.
claims.note: Capability examples do not establish current sales volume or a specific bill of materials.

claims.statement: Watershed markets to toddler nutrition, human snacks and pet nutrition.
The company describes international customers, private label, R&D and commercialization support.
claims.note: No current customer names or revenue mix verified.

claims.statement: Gridley recruiting describes blending, packaging, cold forming, maintenance and shipment coordination.
A dated state staffing schedule includes warehousing. Dedicated cold/frozen storage capacity is not established.
claims.note: Process freezing does not prove a separately operated cold-storage facility.

claims.statement: Watershed’s public directory lists freeze-dried powders, dietary supplements and animal-nutrition offerings.
claims.note: Directory is corroboration for advertised capabilities only. In-house yogurt culturing or dairy processing steps remain unverified.

claims.statement: Watershed’s website claims SQF Level 3 certification and zero safety incidents.
claims.note: Confirmed as a company claim only. Valid certificate, scope, expiry and exhaustive regulatory history not verified.

claims.statement: A July 2009 newspaper excerpt named Kellogg’s as a freeze-dried fruit customer.
claims.note: Full article not retrieved. Do not transfer this relationship to current Kellogg successor entities.

claims.statement: No named current customer was verified to the required standard in this baseline.
claims.note: Use archetypes. Directory document labels, retailer listings and conference attendance do not prove direct supply contracts.

claims.note: Discovery leads only. No extra Watershed-owned facility, supplier or customer node is confirmed from these labels.
